summary: Proxy buffering causes prolonged stream silence then duplicated metadata and split final choice on reconnect
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that long-tail buffering on their corporate proxy results in a silent period mid-stream. The client reconnects and the resumed session receives duplicated metadata events and the final choice is split across two fragments, effectively truncating the last sentence. Impact: Multiple calls from a production webhook pipeline drop the terminal punctuation and sometimes receive a duplicate 'choice_meta' block. This corrupts downstream JSON parsing in their ingestion pipeline and caused a production rollback for one service. Environment: Production calls from ClearView HealthTech, routed through an on-prem NGINX reverse proxy (company-managed) to our hosted Redwood API in us-east-1. Uses SSE streaming for chat completions with model gpt-open-7b-quant and heartbeat enabled every 15s. Steps to reproduce: 1) Configure a reverse proxy with proxy_buffering on and a small proxy_buffer_size so bursts are coalesced (we used nginx with proxy_buffering=on and proxy_buffer_size=4k). 2) Start a streaming chat request that emits a ~3KB terminal packet followed by heartbeat messages. 3) Introduce a short upstream latency spike (150-400ms) that triggers the proxy to flush buffered packets as a single chunk. 4) Simulate client reconnect logic that opens a new SSE session before the previous session's final chunk is fully delivered. Expected: seamless resume with single terminal chunk and intact metadata. Observed: silent period (~6-12s), then client reconnect; the resume delivers two metadata blocks (one repeated) and final text split mid-sentence across the two chunks. Logs/observations: - Request IDs: req-20260310-84a2 / upstream-req-7f1c - Server delivered final chunk at 2026-03-10T15:22:41.972Z. - Proxy flushed combined heartbeat+terminal payload at 2026-03-10T15:22:48.014Z after coalescing. - Client reconnected at 2026-03-10T15:22:49.129Z and received duplicated metadata header. Workaround used by customer: disable proxy_buffering or increase proxy_buffer_size; add client-side guard to wait 3s before issuing reconnect. Next steps: SRE + runtime team to reproduce in our lab with an nginx proxy; consider server-side change to include explicit sequence numbers and terminal flag that survive proxy coalescing. Also evaluate a small SDK change to detect duplicate metadata blocks and stitch split final choices.

investigation_notes: Repro harness: nginx 1.22 with proxy_buffering=on, proxy_buffers=4 4k reproduces duplicate metadata when a final chunk is coalesced with keepalive and then flushed in one packet.

Packet capture shows terminal JSON split boundary moves when proxy appends keepalive bytes before flush, resulting in two JSON fragments sent back-to-back; client reconnect logic can consume both fragments but treats the second metadata block as new.
Hypothesis: Without explicit per-event markers the client cannot disambiguate a buffered-flush duplicate metadata event from a genuine new metadata event on resume.
Mitigation tested: delay reconnect in client by 3s reduces occurrence from 100% to ~2% in our lab; disabling proxy_buffering eliminates the issue.
Runtime mitigation candidate: augment SSE/event stream with 'event_seq' integer and 'terminal': true/false flags in metadata events to allow idempotent resume and reassembly logic.
Impact scope: primarily enterprise customers behind aggressive reverse proxies (on-prem NGINX, some F5 configs). Self-serve customers using cloud front proxies less affected.
Related: SUP-314159 (multiplexed session rotation truncation) shows similar boundary-splitting symptoms but different root cause; cross-referencing for potential common fixes.
resolution: Mitigation in-progress. Short-term guidance provided to customer: increase proxy_buffer_size or disable proxy_buffering and apply client reconnect backoff. Medium-term: runtime PR #12345 to add event_seq + terminal flags submitted; client SDK de-dup patch under review. Will update when PR merges and we validate in staging.
